extracted.intended_audience: journalism researchers, media professionals, policymakers, and news industry stakeholders interested in digital news consumption
extracted.subtask_description: A global survey-based report (Digital News Report 2023) documenting patterns and trends in digital news consumption across 46 markets, providing country-level data, themed chapters (trust, platforms, podcasts, paying for news), methodology, and interactive data tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey sample and market coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: YouGov survey of over 93,000 online news consumers in 46 markets covering half of the world's population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research was conducted by YouGov (and their partners) using an online questionnaire in January and February 2023. The report includes country and market data and enables comparison across markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust and interest in news
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of public interest in news and trust in news — the report notes 'interest and trust in news still falling in many countries'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings are reported at country level (examples: Greece — only 19% trust most news most of the time; Mexico — decline from 50% in 2019 to 36% in 2023; Spain — interest in news has fallen 34 points since 2015). These metrics are used to assess health of news ecosystems and pressure on business models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform and format trends (video-based content and social networks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the growing importance of video-based content distributed via networks such as TikTok, Instagram and YouTube, and the declining influence of legacy platforms such as Facebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report highlights geographic variation (e.g., stronger growth in parts of the Global South). Country examples include South Africa: 50% use TikTok for any purpose and 22% use it for news. This dimension evaluates which platforms/formats people use for news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitudes towards algorithms and their impact on news
rubrics_metrics.description: Public attitudes to algorithms and how algorithms affect news consumption and news environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a themed chapter ('Attitudes towards algorithms and their impact on news' by Richard Fletcher) and functions as a dimension for assessing perceptions and concerns about automated distribution and personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: News participation and online engagement over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Patterns of how people participate in news (e.g., sharing, commenting) and broader online engagement, tracked longitudinally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captured in the chapter 'Unpacking news participation and online engagement over time' (by Kirsten Eddy). Used to evaluate changes in audience behaviour and levels/types of engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources and drivers of news media criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of where criticism of news media comes from and what drives it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented in the chapter 'Sources and drivers of news media criticism' (by Craig T. Robertson). This dimension helps explain declining trust and reputational challenges for outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of public service media
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the role and importance of public service media for individuals and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered in 'The importance of public service media for individuals and for society' (by Rasmus Nielsen and Richard Fletcher). Used as a criterion for judging media systems' capacity to serve public needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: News podcasts: listenership and effective formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Who is listening to news podcasts and which podcast formats are working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter 'News podcasts: who is listening and what formats are working?' (by Nic Newman) evaluates podcast reach and format effectiveness; related resources include a DNR podcast series and downloadable slides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paying for news / subscription and donation behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of who is paying for news content online, which publications people pay for, how much they pay, and their motivations for subscribing or donating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary report titled 'Paying for news: Price-conscious consumers look for value amid cost-of-living crisis' focuses on payment behaviour and motivations; this dimension is used to evaluate business model resilience and consumer willingness to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country and market-level data / interactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of country-specific reports and interactive data tools to explore and compare dimensions and data points between or within countries and markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site offers an interactive 'Build your own charts' tool and country pages for 46 markets; users can download the PDF report and executive summary, and access country-level language reports and local partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear statement of research methods (survey provider, timing, questionnaire mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology section states data were collected by YouGov (and partners) using an online questionnaire in January and February 2023. The report provides methodological notes and links to downloadable materials to allow scrutiny of sampling and fieldwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and supporting resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of ancillary outputs to support interpretation and teaching: podcasts, launch events recordings, slide presentation, and a newsletter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report is disseminated via a DNR podcast series, launch event recordings, slide downloads, and a twice-weekly newsletter; these resources support interpretation, teaching, and wider engagement with findings.
